minutes.headline: Sewer Commission reclassified 380/390 Electric Ave as a warehouse, cutting its connection fee, and approved 400 Electric Ave fees.
minutes.summary: The Commission reclassified 380/390 Electric Ave from a service station to a warehouse, lowering its connection charge and removing a privilege fee. what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission moved to reclassify 380/390 Electric Ave from a service station to a warehouse, lowering its connection fee and removing a privilege fee; the vote result was not audible.
A motion was made to approve the connection and privilege fees for 400 Electric Ave as given in the worksheet; the vote result was not audible.
Release of 400 Electric Ave from the earlier privilege assessment was left to counsel and the buyer's attorney, with a signer authorized before the 15th closing.
The Commission agreed to send businesses a letter on grease trap inspections, stressing education and announcing future inspections.
Whether sewer facilities fall under the town manager's jurisdiction was set for the next agenda, with legal's answer requested in writing.

why_it_matters: Connection and privilege fees are one-time charges set by how a property's use is classified, so a reclassification changes what a property owner pays the sewer system and what the system collects.
Who oversees the sewer department, and whether it falls under the town manager, bears on who sets sewer policy and rates, and may come before residents as articles at town meeting.
watch_next: Counsel's written answer on town manager jurisdiction over sewer facilities, due on the next agenda.
The counsel document releasing 400 Electric Ave from the privilege assessment, needed before the 15th closing.
